title: Brackets, equations and formulas with letters
hook: A copper winding reads 2.0 Ω cold and 2.4 Ω after a run. Using R = R₀(1 + αΔT), how many degrees has it warmed up?
oneBreath: A letter stands for a number, so you can tidy, expand and factorise an expression without changing its value, and trying a number checks every move. With those moves, an equation with a bracket or a fraction is solved by the same undoing you already know, and an inequality's answer is a stretch of the number line. The payoff is writing a job as an equation and turning round a bracket formula such as R = R₀(1 + αΔT), keeping the bracket as one thing.

ideas.title: Like terms
ideas.oneLine: A letter stands for a number, so 3x + 2x makes 5x while 3x + 4 is already finished, and trying a number checks it.

ideas.title: Expanding brackets
ideas.oneLine: Multiply every term inside the bracket, so 3(x + 5) = 3x + 15 and R₀(1 + αΔT) = R₀ + R₀αΔT, and a minus in front changes every sign.

ideas.title: Factorising
ideas.oneLine: Factorising is expanding in reverse, taking out the shared factor: 6x + 15 = 3(2x + 5) and IR₁ + IR₂ + IR₃ = I(R₁ + R₂ + R₃).

ideas.title: Equations with brackets
ideas.oneLine: Solve 3(x − 2) = 27 by dividing first or expanding first, and treat a fraction bar as a bracket, as in (x + 4) ÷ 3 = 5.

ideas.title: Inequalities
ideas.oneLine: An inequality such as x > 3 has a stretch of answers, found with the same undo moves, but multiplying or dividing by a negative flips the sign.

ideas.title: From words to formulas
ideas.oneLine: Write a two-part job as an equation with a bracket, such as 2(x + 3) = 40, then rearrange R = R₀(1 + αΔT) keeping the bracket whole.

calibration.q: Which is the same as 6m − m + 2, whatever number m stands for?
calibration.why: A lone m means one m, so 6m take away one m leaves 5m, and the 2 stays on its own. 6m + 2 treats the lone m as nothing, and 7m wrongly joins the m's with the plain number.

calibration.q: Which is the same as 5(2y − 3), whatever number y stands for?
calibration.why: The 5 multiplies both parts inside: 5 × 2y = 10y and 5 × 3 = 15, so 10y − 15. 10y − 3 forgets to multiply the 3, and −5y then joins the plain 15 to the 10y, which cannot be joined.
